name: Act of February 23, 1889 confirming the Fort Hall agreement for the use of the Lemhi Indians
nations: Shoshone-Bannock Tribes of the Fort Hall Reservation
promises: Royce records that the act confirmed an agreement by the Shoshoni and Bannock of the Fort Hall Reservation to cede a described part of the reservation to the United States for the use of the Lemhi Indians.
today: Royce records that the act was inoperative and never carried into effect because the Lemhi Indians refused to leave their reservation. The Shoshone-Bannock and Lemhi claims before the Indian Claims Commission (Dockets 326-D to 326-I and others) ended in compromise settlements in 1968 and 1971 and were not shown to concern this act.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 928
Shoshone-Bannock Tribes et al. v. United States, Dockets 326-D to 326-H, 366 and 367, Opinion of the Commission on compromise settlement (19 Ind. Cl. Comm. 3, February 13, 1968)
sources.publisher: Indian Claims Commission decisions, Oklahoma State University Library

sources.title: Lemhi Tribe v. United States, Docket 326-I, Opinion on compromise settlement (24 Ind. Cl. Comm. 482, March 8, 1971)
sources.publisher: Indian Claims Commission decisions, Oklahoma State University Library

openQuestions: treaties.json lists the schedule tribes as "Bannock; Coeur d'Alene; Shoshoni". Royce's row for February 23, 1889 names only the "Shoshoni and Bannock of Fort Hall reservation"; Coeur d'Alene appears to come from another row.
The statute text was not opened; the record rests on Royce's summary and note.
